videoIdeas.title: Fancy words don't make you articulate
videoIdeas.hook: You think using big words makes you sound smart. It makes you sound insecure.
videoIdeas.rationale: You already tested this exact idea (the 'most articulate person' post, 477 views) but it flatlined because the caption did the talking and the hook was soft. Public speaking is a core pillar and it's your weakest-performing lane on views — the opportunity is to reframe it as a callout, which is the exact tone that gets you to 6k views on your commentary posts.
videoIdeas.script: You think using big words makes you sound smart. It makes you sound insecure. The most articulate person in the room isn't the one reaching for the thesaurus. It's the one who can take a complicated idea and hand it to you in a sentence you actually understand. That's the whole game. Clarity, not vocabulary. If people have to decode you, you've already lost them. The Prophet peace be upon him spoke in a way a child and a scholar could both follow. Who are you to overcomplicate? Say the thing. Say it plainly. That's what respect sounds like.

visuals.setting: Plain wall or bookshelf, mid-shot, sitting or leaning slightly forward. Muted clothing, calm but sharp energy — you're not shouting, you're correcting.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'STOP USING BIG WORDS' appears as you say the first line, then cuts to a mock 'thesaurus' word being crossed out.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-sentence with no intro, straight into 'It makes you sound insecure.'
Pattern interrupt: hold up a thick book, drop it out of frame as you say 'clarity, not vocabulary.'
On-screen text punchline at the end: 'Say the thing.' held for 2 seconds of silence.

videoIdeas.title: Competent OR trustworthy isn't enough
videoIdeas.hook: Everyone wants to lead. Almost nobody is qualified. Here's the two-word test.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your prophetic-leadership post (508 views, DTauCL6jJ8Z) has strong retention DNA — it's specific and scriptural — but it read like a book quote, not you talking. Leadership is underrepresented in your top posts, and this reframes a proven idea into a punchy standard-setting piece, which suits your voice.
videoIdeas.script: Everyone wants to lead. Almost nobody is qualified. And it's because they only bring half of what's needed. Al-Qawi wal-Ameen. Strong and trustworthy. Competent and honest. Most people you follow are one, not both. The competent one who lies to you. The honest one who's useless in a crisis. Neither should be leading you anywhere. Look at who you're taking direction from right now — in your family, your masjid, your group chats. Are they both? Because if they're not, you've handed your trust to half a leader. Integrity comes first. Competence makes it matter. Anything less is just a personality with a following.

visuals.setting: Standing, plain background, arms free to gesture on the two-word split. Slightly harder energy than idea 1 — this is a standard being set.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text splits the screen in two: 'STRONG' on one side, 'TRUSTWORTHY' on the other, with a hand pointing between them.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the two Arabic words on screen before you speak.
Hold up two fingers, fold one down on 'they only bring half.'
End on a freeze with text: 'Are they both? No? Then why are you following them?'

videoIdeas.title: You're not shy, you're unprepared
videoIdeas.hook: You don't have a fear of public speaking. You have a lack of preparation.
videoIdeas.rationale: lifeofdinoo_ is winning in this exact niche with communication breakdowns ('how to have small talk', 'communication is costing you respect'). You have zero posts attacking the fear-of-speaking angle directly, and it's a gap that your blunt voice can own better than a soft 'tips' account.
videoIdeas.script: You don't have a fear of public speaking. You have a lack of preparation, and you've dressed it up as anxiety so you don't have to fix it. Nobody freezes on a topic they actually know cold. The nerves aren't the enemy. The nerves are information — they're telling you you're not ready. So get ready. Know your first line. Know your last line. Know the three things in between. That's it. Confidence isn't a personality trait you were born without. It's the by-product of having done the work. Stop waiting to feel ready and go and become ready.

visuals.setting: Slightly closer framing, direct to camera, conversational but firm. Could film in a quieter public-ish space to match the 'speaking' theme.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'IT'S NOT FEAR' typed out, then the word 'FEAR' gets replaced with 'PREP' in real time.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-action: you're organising notes/cards, look up and say the line.
Pattern interrupt: mimic a shaky nervous breath, cut, then deliver calmly.
On-screen punchline hold at the end: 'Become ready.'

videoIdeas.title: Stop refuting, start building
videoIdeas.hook: Never a boring day in the Ummah when you lot won't stop tearing each other down.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your callout commentary is what actually moves — the protest post hit 6,134 views and the 'destroyed Iraq' post 2,997. This channels that same energy into your mindset pillar so you're not stuck only reacting to news cycles: a timeless callout about wasting energy on refutation instead of self-improvement.
videoIdeas.script: Never a boring day in the Ummah when you lot won't stop tearing each other down. Everyone's a critic. Everyone's got a refutation. Nobody's actually built anything. Here's the uncomfortable part: it's easier to attack someone else's work than to produce your own. Criticism costs you nothing. Building costs you everything. And that's exactly why most of you choose the keyboard over the effort. Ask yourself honestly — what have you added lately? Not what you've torn down. What have you built? Because the Ummah doesn't need more commentators. It needs people who did the boring, unglamorous work of becoming useful.

visuals.setting: Sitting, direct, unbothered energy — the sharp older brother who's tired of the noise. Neutral background.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'WHAT HAVE YOU BUILT?' flashes, then cuts to you already mid-eyeroll delivering line one.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open with just the question on a black screen for 1 second.
Pattern interrupt: type a fake angry comment on phone, put phone down, address camera.
End card text: 'Criticism is free. Building isn't.'

videoIdeas.title: Not everyone is meant for the mimbar
videoIdeas.hook: Not every student of knowledge is meant to sit in a chair and give Dars.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your own post on this (DatCz6eMZwE, 749 views) had a strong premise but no comments and got buried — the idea deserves a tighter re-cut. It's a leadership/self-worth angle nobody in your competitor set touches, and it lets you speak to the audience's identity instead of the news.
videoIdeas.script: Not every student of knowledge is meant to sit in a chair and give Dars. Not everyone's meant to climb the mimbar, write the books, or lead the prayer. And somewhere along the way we convinced an entire generation that if you're not visibly religious, publicly teaching, loudly leading — then you don't count. That's a lie. The Ummah needs the quiet engineer. The honest businessman. The teacher, the doctor, the father who raises children that don't embarrass the Deen. Leadership isn't a stage. Leadership is being trusted with something and not dropping it. Find your lane and be excellent in it. That's worship too.

visuals.setting: Warmer, slower delivery than the callout videos — this one reassures while it corrects. Softer light, sitting.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text lists roles rapidly — 'Imam / Author / Scholar' — then a big red 'NOT EVERYONE' stamps across them.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the word 'mimbar' with you already speaking.
Quick cut montage of everyday jobs (implied via text) as you name them.
End on text: 'Find your lane. Be excellent. That's worship too.'

videoIdeas.title: Chasing influence before character
videoIdeas.hook: You want the following before you've built the person. That's backwards, and it always collapses.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'influence before character' post (DTauCL6jJ8Z) had real substance. This is timely because birdtart01 and doctordaanish are winning huge on character-and-relationships content right now — it's the proven format in the niche — and your blunt take differentiates you from the softer versions.
videoIdeas.script: You want the following before you've built the person. That's backwards, and it always collapses. We chase influence before character. We want the platform before the substance. And then we wonder why it all falls apart the second real pressure shows up. Character is what holds the weight of influence. Without it, attention just exposes you faster. Every time someone blows up and then implodes, that's not bad luck — that's a small person handed a big platform. So build the person first. Quietly. When nobody's watching. Because if you can't be trusted with a small thing, why would Allah trust you with a big one?

visuals.setting: Direct to camera, steady, low-drama. This one lands harder if you're calm and certain, not hyped.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'INFLUENCE →' with an arrow pointing at a cracking/breaking graphic as you say 'it always collapses.'
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on 'That's backwards.' before any context.
Pattern interrupt: hold up a phone showing a follower count, flip it face-down on 'character holds the weight.'

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your ceiling — 6,134 views, 211 likes, way above your baseline. The reason is the hook: 'Can't believe we're still discussing the necessity of protests in 2026' is timely, opinionated, and puts a stake in the ground in the first line. It gives people a side to agree or argue with, which is why it pulled reach.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 15 comments on 6k views is low for a take this divisive — the caption trails off mid-sentence ('make themselves feel bett') which kills the momentum. End the caption on a direct question or a clean challenge so people feel invited to reply, not just watch.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 24 comments on 2,997 views is your best comment-to-view ratio in the whole set — the Iraq/Afghanistan/Iran framing hits a nerve and people showed up to talk. This is proof your political-clarity angle drives conversation, not just passive views.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The view count is a third of your top post despite similar energy. The caption is all statement, no invitation — pair this kind of take with a leadership or mindset lesson ('here's what this should teach you about who you follow') so it has a second life beyond the news cycle and isn't purely reactive.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 137 likes on 2,106 views is a very high like rate — the 'UAE Hijrah bros' callout is specific, names a real behaviour, and your audience clearly felt seen. Specificity is doing the work here; you named a type of person instead of speaking in generalities.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 5 comments despite the high likes — people agreed but didn't feel a reason to speak. The take is one-directional (you dunking) with no hook back to the audience's own life. Add a turn: 'and before you laugh, ask if you're doing a quieter version of the same thing' — that converts nodding into replies.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: The idea itself is excellent and on-pillar (public speaking) — 'the most articulate person isn't the one who uses fancy words' is a genuinely sharp, teachable point that fits your niche better than the commentary posts.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 477 views and 0 comments — your lowest engagement tier. The problem is the caption IS the whole lesson, so there's nothing left to watch for, and the line is stated softly. Turn it into an accusation ('You think big words make you sound smart') and hold the payoff for the video. This idea deserves a re-shoot with a proper hook.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 58 likes on 508 views is a strong like rate, and this is one of your only true leadership-pillar posts — 'Al-Qawi wal-Ameen, competent and trustworthy' is a memorable, quotable framework that fits your brand exactly.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Reach was low (508) because it opens like a book excerpt ('We often chase influence before character') rather than a person talking. The 📖 and formal formatting make it feel like a carousel caption, not a scroll-stopping video. Lead with the confrontation, deliver the framework in your own blunt voice, and drop the poster-style line breaks.
